title: Learning from Delayed Rewards
summary: Christopher John Cornish Hellaby Watkins submitted his University of Cambridge PhD thesis 'Learning from Delayed Rewards' in May 1989. Watkins's own account states that the thesis described a range of reinforcement-learning algorithms, including one-step Q-learning, and sketched a proof of its convergence.
significance: A documented research milestone for Q-learning in the reinforcement-learning literature, represented here strictly as the May 1989 thesis-submission milestone.

verification.note: Watkins's own thesis page identifies 'Learning from Delayed Rewards' as his Cambridge 1989 PhD thesis and states that it describes reinforcement-learning algorithms including Q-learning. His first-person historical account states that he submitted the thesis in May 1989. The University of Cambridge repository independently identifies Watkins as author and the item as a thesis. May 1989 is therefore recorded only as the thesis-submission milestone; it is not asserted as a universal invention, release, or system-birth date. University of Cambridge is recorded as the thesis institution, not as inferred development geography. No ancestry, influence, causality, or relationship edge is inferred.
